assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organization as a physical-chemical phase transition, a clear underlying principle with quantitative support (liquid-like P granules, nucleoli, multivalent-interaction phase diagrams) and very wide generative reach into cell biology, neurodegeneration and drug discovery. Through a physicist's lens this is the strongest bridge between thermodynamics and living matter.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne published the founding P-granule liquid-droplet work (2009); Rosen's multivalent-protein phase-separation work (2012) gave the quantitative molecular grammar. Pappu and Mittag are strong but a three-person prize is cleaner with these three; the split between founding observation and later theory is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Concept is about 15 years old, widely reproduced and now a standard framework, but the physiological versus in-vitro relevance of many condensates is still debated and the field is partly young.
uncertainties: Debate over whether in-vitro phase separation reflects true in-cell liquid-liquid phase separation.
Fair credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag, and whether the topic is chemistry rather than medicine or physiology.
I am working from my own recall of the literature and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is one of the most widely used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. The principle (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination with tailored ligands) is clear and the practical impact is enormous and unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination, with Kosugi's tin-amide precursor as an earlier step. A two-person citation to Buchwald and Hartwig is defensible and explainable.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, multi-decade, independently reproduced and industrially entrenched. Timing is not an issue, though it follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a sufficiently distinct extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Role of Kosugi and the Migita lineage in the credit story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis changed biology and medicine by dropping the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude; it opened capabilities that were unforeseen. The chemistry core (reversible terminator nucleotides, single-molecule or clustered fluorescence detection) is a concrete invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry; Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Mayer (clustering) and Ju (reversible terminators) are all contested contributions. A clean citation exists but exclusion of Rothberg and others will be controversial.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and ubiquitous for about 20 years; recognition is arguably overdue, but credit is spread across competing platforms.
uncertainties: Competing platform credit (454, Illumina/Solexa, Ju's terminators, Mayer's clusters).
Whether this is a chemistry or a physiology/medicine topic; Sanger sequencing was already honored in 1980.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached silicon-competitive solar efficiency in a decade, with fascinating physics (defect tolerance, long diffusion lengths) and a clear device figure of merit. A strong example of a new material class opening new capability.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers (2009), Park and Snaith drove the solid-state breakthrough (2012); Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are further plausible names. The three chosen give a defensible citation but credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency record and independent reproduction are strong; long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial deployment remain unresolved, so recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercialization remain unproven.
Credit allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure theory and dynamics, with a clean and elegant principle (fictitious electron dynamics via an extended Lagrangian). It enabled first-principles simulation of liquids, interfaces and reactions and remains a foundational tool.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 Car-Parrinello paper is a clear two-person attribution with no real dispute about who did the decisive work.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent use; fully mature and overdue by timeliness, with the theory-and-computation prize (2013) precedent giving mild competition.
uncertainties: Recency of the 2013 computational-chemistry prize may reduce appetite for another simulation topic.
Parrinello also appears in other candidate groupings, so overlap is possible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues created a new pharmacological modality, rewriting what counts as a druggable target. It has large generative potential and a clear mechanistic principle (induced proximity to an E3 ligase).
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTAC-style degraders, Ciulli added VHL-based design and structural rationale; Handa and Ito identified the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism, a key part of molecular glues. A three-person citation must choose between PROTACs and glues.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, with no clearly approved PROTAC, so timing may be premature, though the biochemical principle is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with PROTACs and molecular glues that may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically, a physically elegant measurement that became commercial long-read sequencing and a general single-molecule analytical platform; it appeals to a nanophysicist's sensibilities.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon, Deamer and Branton showed ssDNA translocation (1996); Bayley engineered protein pores, Akeson demonstrated the sequencing route. The right three people are debatable, and I am uncertain about the current status of some credited individuals.
assessment.maturity: Technology is deployed and validated, but the field is still evolving and the credit story is complicated.
uncertainties: Contested attribution among five or more credited people.
Whether recognition should favor the sequencing application or the underlying single-molecule detection principle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnel energy-landscape picture of protein folding is a physical principle that resolved Levinthal's paradox and shaped how chemists think about folding, frustration and association-drive structure. It connects directly to non-equilibrium statistical physics.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill are the central theorists of the landscape and hydrophobic-collapse views; Bryngelson shared early credit and Fersht experimentally tested the landscape. A clean split between theory and experiment is hard.
assessment.maturity: Concept is mature and widely accepted, but the 2024 protein prize partially addressed the folding problem, and the theory's direct predictive power is conceptual rather than technological.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 protein prize and between theoretical and experimental credit.
Unresolved priority among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and Bryngelson.
